title: The Static of Station Meridian
premise: Ivo Vane, a navigator for the scrappy Meridian Line, discovers her dead sister's name on the manifest of the Halcyon, a ship that vanished a decade ago and never flew again. The manifest is a forgery — but both the Concord fleet and the Breakaway Syndicate believe it proves the Halcyon's lost colony ship, and its sleeping colonists, still drift in contested space, and each side will start a war to claim them. Ivo must keep the forgery alive long enough to find the Halcyon's real fate, discovering her sister survived the wreck as one of the cold-sleep 'backups' Ivo has hauled for years. In the end, Ivo broadcasts the truth — that the colonists woke years ago and built their own quiet life — forcing both fleets to stand down, though it costs her the Meridian and nearly her life, and leaves her with a found family among the woken instead of the sister she mourned.
about_author: Mirabel Ashgrove is a former radio operator who spent six years on remote northern stations, where static and silence shaped her ear for lonely voices across vast distances. She writes science fiction about people who keep systems running when no one is watching.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ivo Vane's POV. Routine cargo audit on Station Meridian turns up the Halcyon's manifest bearing her sister Sefa's name — on a ship lost ten years ago. Ivo hides the file, terrified and electrified. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by an impossible hope she doesn't dare trust.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She investigates the cold-sleep 'backup' containers she's hauled for years, learning they're people — and that Meridian Line captain Oduya has been quietly protecting them. A Concord inspector arrives asking about the Halcyon. Beat: complicity deepens into loyalty; the lie begins.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Concord inspector Rhee and Syndicate broker Kess, each convinced the manifest proves the colony ship lives. Both converge on Meridian. Ivo realizes her hidden file is now the fuse. Beat: dread — her private grief has become a public weapon.

chapters.title: What Oduya Knew
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Oduya confesses the Meridian has carried woken colonists to safety for years, Sefa possibly among them, and begs Ivo to let the lie die. Ivo refuses: the truth means war before anyone is safe. Beat: found family tested against the price of survival.

chapters.title: The Long Orbit
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She pilots a decoy run to buy time, faking the Halcyon's trail into empty space while Rhee shadows her. Kess's Syndicate escort forces a near-collision. Beat: competence under pressure; Ivo becomes the keeper of a story both fleets would kill for.

chapters.title: Signal from the Wreck
chapters.summary: Rhee's POV. Rhee decodes an old distress fragment proving the Halcyon broke apart — but also that lifepods launched toward an unlisted moon. Torn between duty and conscience, Rhee withholds it from Concord command. Beat: the inspector becomes a co-conspirator.

chapters.title: Sefa
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following Rhee's fragment, Ivo reaches the moon and finds the woken colony — and Sefa, alive, older, and furious that Ivo's forged manifest has painted a target on them. Beat: reunion curdled by guilt; love that cannot undo the damage.

chapters.title: The Fleet at the Door
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Syndicate warships arrive at the moon, with Concord close behind. Kess, learning the colonists want only to be left alone, hesitates — his own family once fled Concord. Beat: the antagonist's humanity surfaces as countdown to war.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax. Using the Meridian's aging array, Ivo transmits everything — the wreck, the colony, the forgery, her confession — to both fleets at once, betting that truth shames them into standing down. Oduya dies shielding the array. Beat: sacrifice; the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: The Static After
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, resolution. The fleets withdraw into uneasy negotiation; the colony gains recognition through Rhee's testimony and Kess's brokerage. Ivo, stripped of her license, stays on the moon — not as Sefa's sister returned, but as a new member of a family that chose her. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
